issues.description: Default speaker for bulbul:v3-beta contradicts documented contract (aditya vs shubh)
issues.detail: The module docstring, class docstring, and PR description all promise `aditya` as the v3-beta default speaker. The TTS_MODEL_CONFIGS entry sets default_speaker="shubh". This is a contract violation between specification and implementation: callers relying on the documented default get a different voice. Pick one and make them agree.

issues.description: Pace clamping silently weakens the postcondition of the InputParams contract
issues.detail: InputParams declares pace with Field(ge=0.3, le=3.0), which is the supertype contract callers see. For v3-beta the implementation narrows the accepted range to 0.5-2.0 and silently clamps. The subtype (v3 config) strengthens the precondition without telling the caller through the type. Either raise ValueError or split InputParams per model so the contract reflects reality.

issues.description: Incompatible-parameter detection compares against defaults, conflating intent with default
issues.detail: Code uses `params.pitch != 0.0`, `params.loudness != 1.0`, `params.temperature != 0.6` to decide whether a caller "used" an unsupported parameter. A caller who explicitly passes the default value gets no warning; a caller who wants the default is indistinguishable from one who omitted it. The contract should distinguish unset (None sentinel) from set-to-default, or validate strictly like the STT side does.

issues.description: STT and TTS apply opposite enforcement policies for unsupported parameters
issues.detail: SarvamSTTService raises ValueError when an unsupported prompt/mode/language is passed; SarvamHttpTTSService merely logs a warning and silently drops pitch/loudness/temperature when unsupported. Two services in the same package should not present opposite contracts for the same situation. Pick one substitution discipline (strict raise, or documented best-effort) and apply it uniformly.

issues.description: get_speakers_for_model silently falls back to v2 speakers for unknown models
issues.detail: The helper returns v2 speakers for any unrecognized model name. That is a leaky abstraction: callers cannot tell "unknown model" from "v2 model" by the return value. Prefer raising ValueError (matching __init__ behavior) or returning an empty list so the contract is unambiguous.

issues.description: Model dispatch keyed by string literals instead of the SarvamTTSModel enum just introduced
issues.detail: The PR adds SarvamTTSModel enum for type safety, then keys TTS_MODEL_CONFIGS and all comparisons by raw strings ("bulbul:v2", "bulbul:v3-beta"). The enum becomes documentation rather than a typed boundary. Either key configs by the enum and accept enum-or-str in __init__, or drop the enum. A type that exists only as a label is not an abstraction.

review.summary: The PR makes a real abstraction improvement: ModelConfig / TTSModelConfig as frozen dataclasses pull model-specific capabilities behind a clean record, replacing fragile substring checks. The module boundary is largely correct and the STT subtype audit is clean. However, the TTS side has contract problems: a documented default speaker that disagrees with code, silent pace clamping that violates the InputParams range contract, and warning-vs-raise enforcement that is inconsistent with the STT module's strict validation. The newly added SarvamTTSModel enum is decorative — dispatch still keys on raw strings. Fix the contract drift between docstrings, types, and runtime before merge; the architectural direction is right.
